Both blind agents independently answered 'entailed' citing 'subalternation' (All A are B implies Some A are B), a named, historically standard Aristotelian inference rule. My gold label ('unknown') instead follows modern predicate logic, which does not assume a universal statement's subject class is nonempty. Both agents' own English translations were accurate, so this isn't a translation failure -- it's a case where the item's gold label depends on which of two legitimate logical traditions is assumed, which the item didn't specify. This is a dataset-design caveat on my part, not necessarily a genuine model deficiency.
